destination.name: Namadgi National Park
destination.tagline: Bush walks, historic huts and Aboriginal rock art across the ACT's high country.
destination.description: Namadgi covers about 46% of the Australian Capital Territory, a mountain landscape of granite tors, waterfalls and snow-capped ranges south-west of Canberra. Walks lead to granite outcrops, 19th-century settlers' huts and Aboriginal rock art, and the Honeysuckle Creek site recalls the Apollo moon landing broadcasts. The visitor centre is on Naas Road near Tharwa village, the park's gateway.
whyVisit: See the drop at Gibraltar Falls
See Aboriginal rock art at Yankee Hat

goodToKnow.title: Start at the visitor centre
goodToKnow.detail: The Namadgi Visitor Centre on Naas Road near Tharwa has track information and track conditions. Check its opening hours before you go.

goodToKnow.title: Book Corin Forest ahead
goodToKnow.detail: The Corin Forest alpine slide and snowplay need advance booking and open on limited days in much of the year. Check the operator's calendar.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Walk the tracks in {months}, when days are mild. Winter brings cold and snowplay.
